title: Verb + -ing or to ... 2 (try, need, help)
subtitle: try to do / try doing; need to do / need doing
summary: Tell apart try to do (attempt) and try doing (experiment), need to do and need doing (= need to be done), and use can't help doing.

lesson.heading: try to do = attempt
lesson.text: **Try to do** = attempt to do, make an effort to do something.

examples.text: I was very tired. I **tried to keep** my eyes open, but I couldn't.
Please **try to be** quiet when you come home. Everyone will be asleep.

lesson.heading: try something / try doing = experiment
lesson.text: **Try something** or **try doing something** = do it as an experiment or test, to see if it helps or if you like it.

examples.text: These cakes are delicious. You should **try one**.
examples.note: = have one to see if you like it

examples.text: We couldn't find anywhere to stay. We **tried every hotel** in the town, but they were all full.
examples.note: = we went to every hotel to see if they had a room

examples.text: *A:* The photocopier doesn't seem to be working. *B:* **Try pressing** the green button.
examples.note: = press the green button - perhaps this will help to solve the problem

left.label: tried to move
left.text: I made an effort, but I couldn't do it.
examples: I **tried to move** the table, but it was too heavy. (so I couldn't move it)

right.label: tried moving
right.text: I did it, as an experiment, to see if it looked better.
examples: I didn't like the way the furniture was arranged, so I **tried moving** the table to the other side of the room. But it didn't look right, so I moved it back again.

left.label: I need to do something
left.text: = it is necessary for me to do it.
examples: He **needs to work** harder if he wants to make progress.
I don't **need to come** to the meeting, do I?

right.label: something needs doing
examples: My phone **needs charging**. (= it needs to be charged)
Does your suit **need cleaning**? (= ... need to be cleaned)
It's a difficult problem. It **needs thinking** about carefully.

lesson.heading: help and can't help
lesson.text: You can say **help to do** or **help do** (with or without to). But **I can't help doing something** = I can't stop myself doing it.

examples.text: Everybody **helped to clean** up after the party.
Can you **help me move** this table?
examples.note: or Can you help me to move ...

examples.text: I don't like him, but he has a lot of problems. I **can't help feeling** sorry for him.
She tried to be serious, but she **couldn't help laughing**.
I'm sorry I'm so nervous. I **can't help it**.

lesson.text: If the effort failed or was hard, it is try to do. If you did it easily to see what would happen, it is try doing.

exercises.prompt: I tried ___ the shelf, but I wasn't tall enough.
exercises.explanation: An attempt that failed: tried to reach.

exercises.prompt: I rang the doorbell, but there was no answer. Then I tried ___ on the window, but there was still no answer.
exercises.explanation: An experiment to see if it would help: tried knocking.

exercises.prompt: Is try used as an attempt (try to do) or as an experiment (try doing)?
categories: try to do = attempt, make an effort
try doing = do it as an experiment

items.text: I tried to keep my eyes open, but I couldn't.
We tried to put the fire out, but without success.
She tried asking Carl, but he didn't have any money.
Please leave me alone. I'm trying to concentrate.
Mr Bennett isn't here. Please try calling later.

exercises.prompt: If you have a problem with the computer, try ___ it.
exercises.explanation: Do it as an experiment to solve the problem: try restarting it.

exercises.prompt: The grass is very long. It ___.
exercises.explanation: Something needs doing = it needs to be done: It needs cutting.
They need to be tightened: They need tightening.

exercises.prompt: My grandmother isn't able to look after herself any more. She needs ___ after.
exercises.explanation: She needs to be looked after: needs looking after.

exercises.prompt: I can't make a decision right now. I need ___ about it.
exercises.explanation: It is necessary for me to do it: I need to think about it.

exercises.prompt: That shirt looks fine. It doesn't need ___.
exercises.explanation: The shirt does not need to be ironed: doesn't need ironing. (But: You don't need to iron it.)

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order. You feel sorry for him although you don't like him.
exercises.answer: I can't help feeling sorry for him.
exercises.explanation: can't help + -ing = can't stop myself: can't help feeling.

exercises.prompt: He looks so funny. Whenever I see him, I can't help ___.
exercises.explanation: can't help doing = can't stop myself doing it: can't help smiling.

exercises.statement: She tried to be serious, but she couldn't help to laugh.
exercises.explanation: She couldn't help laughing. After can't help we use -ing.
